## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: it routes Qwen3.8's 512-expert softmax MoE router through aiter's `topk_gating` instead of the vendored `vllm::moe::topkGatingSoftmax` launcher it reaches today, worth **+1.48%** output tok/s without MTP and **+2.22%** with NEXTN MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes. This PR needs [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) (merged, not yet in SGLang's aiter pin).

On SGLang v0.5.20 at the default page size the gain is +1.03% without MTP and +0.40% with MTP; see https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40708#issuecomment-5933064541. 

Qwen3.8 picks 10 experts out of 512 on every one of its 92 layers. On ROCm that pick is 0.878 ms per decode step, 4.8% of decode kernel time, against 0.440 ms/step on B300. `aiter.fused_moe.fused_topk` only hands off to its ASM router for `(experts, topk)` in `(128,4), (128,6), (128,8), (256,6), (256,8), (384,8), (640,8)`, and Qwen3.8 is `(512, 10)`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has the same `(512, 10)` softmax router at hidden size 2560 and takes the same path.

[#28399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28399) tried the same wiring in August and got nothing for it (ITL +3.7%, throughput -1.9% on Qwen3.5 TP2). aiter has since gained the E=512 kernel and learned to honour `need_renorm` for softmax ([Rocm/aiter4460](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4460)).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: `_use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax()` decides, and the `_use_aiter` softmax branch calls `topk_gating` when it says yes. Every other shape keeps `aiter_fused_topk`.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, default on, as the kill switch.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen38_moe_softmax_topk_gating.py`: agreement with the legacy launcher at 4, 128 and 1024 rows at hidden sizes 8192 and 2560, plus every envelope boundary.

The dispatch: gfx95, AITER on, hidden size 8192 (Qwen3.8) or 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), BF16 hidden states, BF16 contiguous gating output, 512 experts, at most 4096 rows, no correction bias, no fused shared slots, no packed output.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X node, TP8, SGLang v0.5.19. GSM8K is 5-shot, 1314 items, thinking on. NIAH is `niah_single_2` at 65,536 / 131,072.

| Arm | GSM8K | NIAH 65k / 131k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP baseline | 0.978 | 0.998 / 1.000 |
| MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.990 / 1.00 |
| non-MTP baseline | 0.979 | 0.998 / 0.998 |
| non-MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.998 / 0.994 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, `chunked-prefill-size 16384, page-size 64`. 12 cells per arm: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16. Geomeans of output tok/s. 

The four arms ran on the same node and differ only in which kernel the softmax router call reaches:

- **baseline**: v0.5.19 as released. Every router call goes through `aiter_fused_topk`, which for `(512, 10)` lands on the vendored `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling**: this PR without the 4096-row limit. Every router call, including the 16384-token prefill chunks, goes to `topk_gating`. Above 1024 rows `topk_gating` switches from the E=512 kernel to a shared-memory kernel, which loses to `topkGatingSoftmax` above 4096 rows (see the microbenchmark below).
- **this PR**: `topk_gating` up to 4096 rows, which covers decode, verify, draft-extend and short prefill chunks. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) sends 512-expert softmax routing to a Triton kernel, but only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and at most 128 rows, so on main it never fires for Qwen3.8. For this arm its gate was widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows, enough for every decode and verify step in this sweep. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0142 | 0.9872 |
| **this PR** | **1.0148** | 0.9859 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0160 | 0.9891 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~4.00 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0211 | ~4.00 | 0.9906 |
| **this PR** | **1.0222** | ~4.00 | 1.0009 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0199 | ~4.00 | 0.9966 |

On v0.5.19 at page size 64, MTP gains more because verify and draft-extend add router launches per accepted token. On v0.5.20 at the default page size it gains less. Decode, verify and draft run in CUDA graphs; prefill runs eager (`prefill.backend='disabled'` in the server log, confirmed in the traces).

The #39986 Triton arm lands within 0.25% of this PR in both modes (0.12% above without MTP, 0.23% below with MTP), inside run-to-run spread, so end to end the two routers tie on Qwen3.8. The microbenchmark below shows where each kernel is faster and why this PR uses `topk_gating`.

End to end, the ceiling is worth 0.06% without MTP and 0.11% with it, inside run-to-run spread, so the case for it rests on the kernel census. Concurrency 4, TP0 trace, router launches (one per layer per forward):

| Arm | Cell | `topkGatingSoftmax` | E=512 kernel | aiter smem | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 8k/100 | 9476 | 0 | 0 | 9476 |
| baseline | 60k/100 | 10580 | 0 | 0 | 10580 |
| no ceiling | 8k/100 | 0 | 9200 | 276 | 9476 |
| no ceiling | 60k/100 | 0 | 9202 | 1380 | 10582 |
| **with ceiling** | 8k/100 | 276 | 9200 | 0 | 9476 |
| **with ceiling** | 60k/100 | 1380 | 9201 | 0 | 10581 |

Without a ceiling the prefill chunks (3 x 92 at 8k, 15 x 92 at 60k) land on aiter's slower shared-memory kernel; with it they go back to the legacy launcher and decode keeps the E=512 kernel.

Microbenchmark, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 14.70 | **11.47** | 20.50 | 9.26 | 4.74 | **4.20** |
| 1024 | 15.56 | **12.28** | 21.18 | 9.42 | 5.50 | **4.75** |
| 2048 | 15.57 | **11.98** | 21.18 | 9.44 | 9.73 | **6.57** |
| 4096 | 15.53 | **12.00** | 21.61 | 11.50 | 11.63 | **10.78** |
| 5120 | 14.86 | **12.53** | 20.66 | **11.51** | 12.92 | 12.66 |
| 6144 | 15.02 | **13.68** | 20.82 | **11.58** | 14.10 | 14.55 |
| 7168 | **14.88** | 15.16 | 20.84 | **11.58** | 15.18 | 15.95 |
| 8192 | **14.89** | 16.55 | 20.85 | **11.64** | 16.51 | 17.93 |
| 16384 | **18.74** | 28.20 | 32.30 | **18.56** | 28.58 | 32.60 |

Graph times approximate kernel GPU time; eager times include launch overhead. On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.92 vs 11.51 us, 28.58 vs 18.56 at 16384). Eager it stays ahead through 6144. The ceiling is 4096, the largest size where it is within noise on GPU time and still ahead eager.

Why `topk_gating` rather than extending #39986 to Qwen3.8. Under CUDA graphs the Triton kernel is the fastest of the three, 0.5-0.75 us per call up to 1024 rows. Decode, verify and draft replay from graphs, so that lead is real, but it is small next to a decode step: in the TP0 traces Triton saves 9-20 us per graph replay of 7.7-14.2 ms, 0.1-0.15% of GPU time, which is why the end-to-end numbers above tie.

Where they differ is eager. Triton is the slowest of the three there (about 21 us per call, against 12 us for `topk_gating` and 15 us for `topkGatingSoftmax`), but those times are mostly launch overhead, so this matters only for prefills short enough to be launch-bound, which this sweep did not measure.

The two PRs don't conflict. #39986 fires only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and this PR only at 8192 (Qwen3.8) and 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). 

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), `topk_gating` falls back to a generic kernel at 8.0-9.2 us in graphs through 1024 rows, barely ahead of legacy.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, measured by @amd-nprotaso in review: output tok/s +2.17%, median TPOT 7.71 -> 7.54 ms (-2.25%). Accept length came out 0.7% higher on the patch side, so per decode step the gain is -1.4% (17.84 -> 17.59 ms). 

Not measured: other 512-expert models, which keep their current dispatch; short-prompt prefill (chunks <= 4096 rows) end to end; gfx942; anything outside TP8/EP1.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing docs change; the new env var is documented at its definition in `environ.py`, next to the other AITER switches.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

## v0.5.20 at the default page size

This PR rerun on SGLang v0.5.20 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x`) at the default page size (1), with `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` and `--disable-radix-cache`. 8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4. Same 12 cells as the description: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16.

- **baseline**: stock v0.5.20.[Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), on the same node as the baseline. Server arguments are identical apart from `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING=1`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: stock v0.5.20 plus #39986's router, with its gate widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows. It ran on a second MI355X node against a stock v0.5.20 rerun on that node, so its row is the ratio to that rerun. Stock differs by 0.26% without MTP and 0.01% with MTP between the two nodes.

MTP arms also carry #39064 and #39069 so NEXTN loads this checkpoint. Ratios are candidate / baseline geomeans over the 12 cells. TTFT is median TTFT, so below 1.0 is faster.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| **this PR** | **1.0103** | 1.0000 |
| #39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0129 | 0.9990 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~3.99 | 1.0000 |
| **this PR** | **1.0040** | ~3.99 | 0.9912 |
| #39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0051 | ~3.99 | 1.0039 |

Accept length is 3.979-3.997 per cell for this PR's pair (mean 3.987 baseline, 3.985 this PR) and 3.976-3.998 for the Triton pair (mean 3.984 stock, 3.986 Triton).

What differs from the v0.5.19 numbers in the description (page size 64, +1.48% / +2.22%):

- The gain is smaller, and MTP now gains less than non-MTP (+0.40% against +1.03%). A likely reason is that the MTP step is longer at page size 1, so the same per-step router saving is a smaller share of it. This has not been profiled.
- The Triton arm is 0.26% above this PR without MTP and 0.11% above with MTP. That is the same size as the stock difference between the two nodes, so the two routers still tie end to end.
- The no-ceiling arm and the kernel-count table were not rerun. They are v0.5.19 only.

Microbenchmark on v0.5.20, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.00 | **11.77** | 20.73 | 9.36 | 4.76 | **4.08** |
| 1024 | 15.48 | **12.07** | 20.64 | 9.40 | 5.48 | **4.76** |
| 2048 | 15.18 | **12.28** | 20.86 | 9.46 | 9.67 | **6.54** |
| 4096 | 15.09 | **12.25** | 20.73 | 11.43 | 11.55 | **10.63** |
| 5120 | 15.20 | **12.49** | 20.76 | **11.46** | 12.86 | 12.58 |
| 6144 | 15.20 | **13.78** | 20.83 | **11.62** | 14.14 | 14.74 |
| 7168 | 15.25 | 15.18 | 20.64 | **11.60** | 15.41 | 16.64 |
| 8192 | **15.15** | 16.42 | 20.65 | **11.83** | 16.96 | 18.52 |
| 16384 | **19.11** | 28.64 | 32.37 | **18.67** | 28.85 | 32.81 |

The v0.5.19 conclusions hold:

- On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.86 vs 11.46 us, 28.85 vs 18.67 at 16384).
- Eager, it stays ahead through 6144 and ties legacy at 7168 (15.18 vs 15.25 us, within run-to-run spread).
- Under graphs, Triton leads `topk_gating` by about 0.7 us per call up to 1024 rows.

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) (the stock v0.5.20 image), graph `topk_gating` is 8.04 / 9.23 / 9.66 / 11.65 us at 1 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 rows, so the generic-kernel fallback is unchanged. Legacy and Triton in that image match the table above within 0.6 us.

## v0.5.21 with aiter main and fused shared experts

On v0.5.21 with aiter main and #41899's fused shared expert, this PR gives +1.50% output throughput without MTP and +0.71% with MTP. On v0.5.20 it was +1.03% / +0.40%. 

Setup: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x`, aiter main `a786bda2` (it has [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) and [Rocm/aiter5835](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5835), so no aiter patch), #41899 with `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`, and #39069 for NEXTN. 8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, page size 1, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`, `--disable-radix-cache`, same 12 cells as the description. Both arms ran on one node. The only difference is this PR plus `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING=1`. MTP arms use `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` with `SGLANG_AITER_HONOR_EXPLICIT_MEM_FRACTION=1`, non-MTP uses 0.9. The baseline router is `topkGatingSoftmax`. #39986's Triton router is in v0.5.21 but fires only at hidden size 4096 and at most 128 rows, so not for this model.

Ratios are this PR / baseline, geomean over the 12 cells:

| Mode | out tok/s | median TTFT | median ITL | accept length (baseline / this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| non-MTP | **1.0150** | 0.9953 | 0.9766 | - |
| NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens | **1.0071** | 0.9800 | 0.9903 | 3.988 / 3.985 |

- Without MTP, this PR is ahead in all 12 cells, from +4.6% at 8k/1k concurrency 4 to +0.3% at 60k/600 concurrency 64.
- With MTP, it is ahead in 10 of 12 cells, up to +3.8% at 8k/1k concurrency 4. The other two (8k/1k concurrency 256, 60k/600 concurrency 64) are -0.1%, within run-to-run spread.
- The gain is larger than on v0.5.20, but the kernel did not get faster: graph legacy and graph `topk_gating` match the v0.5.20 times within 0.15 us. 
- Fusion: on ROCm, Qwen appends the shared slot after top-k (`fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights`, which also computes the shared gate). The router logits stay 512 wide, `TopK` has no fused shared experts, and `topk_gating` runs.

Microbenchmark on v0.5.21 with aiter main, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router as it ships in v0.5.21. 5120 to 7168 rows were not rerun.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.57 | **12.70** | 24.41 | 9.22 | **4.75** | 4.99 |
| 1024 | 16.12 | **13.13** | 24.94 | 9.36 | **5.46** | 5.53 |
| 2048 | 16.07 | **12.97** | 24.87 | 9.47 | 9.66 | **7.25** |
| 4096 | 16.04 | **13.08** | 24.83 | 11.57 | 11.60 | **11.41** |
| 8192 | **15.97** | 16.62 | 24.94 | **11.72** | 16.81 | 19.56 |
| 16384 | **19.00** | 28.48 | 34.16 | **18.72** | 29.49 | 35.16 |

- Under graphs, `topk_gating` beats legacy through 1024 rows, is within 0.2 us at 2048 and 4096, and loses from 8192. The 4096-row ceiling stays.
- Eager, it beats legacy through 4096 rows and loses at 8192.
- Triton is 0.7 to 0.9 us slower under graphs than on v0.5.20, so `topk_gating` now leads it through 1024 rows. Triton still leads at 2048 and 4096.
- Routed weights match legacy within 1.2e-7. Above 1024 rows a few ids differ, only where two experts tie on the same bf16 score at the top-10 edge.

detail.body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: it routes Qwen3.8's 512-expert softmax MoE router through aiter's `topk_gating` instead of the vendored `vllm::moe::topkGatingSoftmax` launcher it reaches today, worth **+1.48%** output tok/s without MTP and **+2.22%** with NEXTN MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes. This PR needs [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) (merged, not yet in SGLang's aiter pin).

On SGLang v0.5.20 at the default page size the gain is +1.03% without MTP and +0.40% with MTP; see https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40708#issuecomment-5933064541. 

Qwen3.8 picks 10 experts out of 512 on every one of its 92 layers. On ROCm that pick is 0.878 ms per decode step, 4.8% of decode kernel time, against 0.440 ms/step on B300. `aiter.fused_moe.fused_topk` only hands off to its ASM router for `(experts, topk)` in `(128,4), (128,6), (128,8), (256,6), (256,8), (384,8), (640,8)`, and Qwen3.8 is `(512, 10)`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has the same `(512, 10)` softmax router at hidden size 2560 and takes the same path.

[#28399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28399) tried the same wiring in August and got nothing for it (ITL +3.7%, throughput -1.9% on Qwen3.5 TP2). aiter has since gained the E=512 kernel and learned to honour `need_renorm` for softmax ([Rocm/aiter4460](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4460)).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: `_use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax()` decides, and the `_use_aiter` softmax branch calls `topk_gating` when it says yes. Every other shape keeps `aiter_fused_topk`.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, default on, as the kill switch.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen38_moe_softmax_topk_gating.py`: agreement with the legacy launcher at 4, 128 and 1024 rows at hidden sizes 8192 and 2560, plus every envelope boundary.

The dispatch: gfx95, AITER on, hidden size 8192 (Qwen3.8) or 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), BF16 hidden states, BF16 contiguous gating output, 512 experts, at most 4096 rows, no correction bias, no fused shared slots, no packed output.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X node, TP8, SGLang v0.5.19. GSM8K is 5-shot, 1314 items, thinking on. NIAH is `niah_single_2` at 65,536 / 131,072.

| Arm | GSM8K | NIAH 65k / 131k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP baseline | 0.978 | 0.998 / 1.000 |
| MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.990 / 1.00 |
| non-MTP baseline | 0.979 | 0.998 / 0.998 |
| non-MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.998 / 0.994 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, `chunked-prefill-size 16384, page-size 64`. 12 cells per arm: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16. Geomeans of output tok/s. 

The four arms ran on the same node and differ only in which kernel the softmax router call reaches:

- **baseline**: v0.5.19 as released. Every router call goes through `aiter_fused_topk`, which for `(512, 10)` lands on the vendored `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling**: this PR without the 4096-row limit. Every router call, including the 16384-token prefill chunks, goes to `topk_gating`. Above 1024 rows `topk_gating` switches from the E=512 kernel to a shared-memory kernel, which loses to `topkGatingSoftmax` above 4096 rows (see the microbenchmark below).
- **this PR**: `topk_gating` up to 4096 rows, which covers decode, verify, draft-extend and short prefill chunks. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) sends 512-expert softmax routing to a Triton kernel, but only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and at most 128 rows, so on main it never fires for Qwen3.8. For this arm its gate was widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows, enough for every decode and verify step in this sweep. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0142 | 0.9872 |
| **this PR** | **1.0148** | 0.9859 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0160 | 0.9891 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~4.00 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0211 | ~4.00 | 0.9906 |
| **this PR** | **1.0222** | ~4.00 | 1.0009 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0199 | ~4.00 | 0.9966 |

On v0.5.19 at page size 64, MTP gains more because verify and draft-extend add router launches per accepted token. On v0.5.20 at the default page size it gains less. Decode, verify and draft run in CUDA graphs; prefill runs eager (`prefill.backend='disabled'` in the server log, confirmed in the traces).

The #39986 Triton arm lands within 0.25% of this PR in both modes (0.12% above without MTP, 0.23% below with MTP), inside run-to-run spread, so end to end the two routers tie on Qwen3.8. The microbenchmark below shows where each kernel is faster and why this PR uses `topk_gating`.

End to end, the ceiling is worth 0.06% without MTP and 0.11% with it, inside run-to-run spread, so the case for it rests on the kernel census. Concurrency 4, TP0 trace, router launches (one per layer per forward):

| Arm | Cell | `topkGatingSoftmax` | E=512 kernel | aiter smem | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 8k/100 | 9476 | 0 | 0 | 9476 |
| baseline | 60k/100 | 10580 | 0 | 0 | 10580 |
| no ceiling | 8k/100 | 0 | 9200 | 276 | 9476 |
| no ceiling | 60k/100 | 0 | 9202 | 1380 | 10582 |
| **with ceiling** | 8k/100 | 276 | 9200 | 0 | 9476 |
| **with ceiling** | 60k/100 | 1380 | 9201 | 0 | 10581 |

Without a ceiling the prefill chunks (3 x 92 at 8k, 15 x 92 at 60k) land on aiter's slower shared-memory kernel; with it they go back to the legacy launcher and decode keeps the E=512 kernel.

Microbenchmark, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 14.70 | **11.47** | 20.50 | 9.26 | 4.74 | **4.20** |
| 1024 | 15.56 | **12.28** | 21.18 | 9.42 | 5.50 | **4.75** |
| 2048 | 15.57 | **11.98** | 21.18 | 9.44 | 9.73 | **6.57** |
| 4096 | 15.53 | **12.00** | 21.61 | 11.50 | 11.63 | **10.78** |
| 5120 | 14.86 | **12.53** | 20.66 | **11.51** | 12.92 | 12.66 |
| 6144 | 15.02 | **13.68** | 20.82 | **11.58** | 14.10 | 14.55 |
| 7168 | **14.88** | 15.16 | 20.84 | **11.58** | 15.18 | 15.95 |
| 8192 | **14.89** | 16.55 | 20.85 | **11.64** | 16.51 | 17.93 |
| 16384 | **18.74** | 28.20 | 32.30 | **18.56** | 28.58 | 32.60 |

Graph times approximate kernel GPU time; eager times include launch overhead. On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.92 vs 11.51 us, 28.58 vs 18.56 at 16384). Eager it stays ahead through 6144. The ceiling is 4096, the largest size where it is within noise on GPU time and still ahead eager.

Why `topk_gating` rather than extending #39986 to Qwen3.8. Under CUDA graphs the Triton kernel is the fastest of the three, 0.5-0.75 us per call up to 1024 rows. Decode, verify and draft replay from graphs, so that lead is real, but it is small next to a decode step: in the TP0 traces Triton saves 9-20 us per graph replay of 7.7-14.2 ms, 0.1-0.15% of GPU time, which is why the end-to-end numbers above tie.

Where they differ is eager. Triton is the slowest of the three there (about 21 us per call, against 12 us for `topk_gating` and 15 us for `topkGatingSoftmax`), but those times are mostly launch overhead, so this matters only for prefills short enough to be launch-bound, which this sweep did not measure.

The two PRs don't conflict. #39986 fires only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and this PR only at 8192 (Qwen3.8) and 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). 

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), `topk_gating` falls back to a generic kernel at 8.0-9.2 us in graphs through 1024 rows, barely ahead of legacy.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, measured by @amd-nprotaso in review: output tok/s +2.17%, median TPOT 7.71 -> 7.54 ms (-2.25%). Accept length came out 0.7% higher on the patch side, so per decode step the gain is -1.4% (17.84 -> 17.59 ms).

+"""ROCm coverage for the 512-expert softmax router on aiter `topk_gating`."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe import topk as topk_module
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=10, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+# Qwen3.8 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
+HIDDEN_SIZES = (8192, 2560)
+NUM_EXPERTS = 512
+TOPK = 10
+
+
+def _envelope(
+    gating_output,
+    hidden_size,
+    correction_bias=None,
+    num_fused_shared_experts=0,
+    packed_out=None,
+    hidden_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+):
+    hidden_states = torch.empty(
+        gating_output.shape[0],
+        hidden_size,
+        device=gating_output.device,
+        dtype=hidden_dtype,
+    )
+    return topk_module._use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax(
+        hidden_states,
+        gating_output,
+        correction_bias,
+        num_fused_shared_experts,
+        packed_out,
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip and is_gfx95_supported(),
+    "requires AMD gfx95",
+)
+class TestQwen38MoeSoftmaxTopKGating(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_topk_gating_matches_legacy_launcher(self):
+        from aiter.fused_moe import fused_topk as aiter_fused_topk
+
+        for hidden_size, num_tokens in itertools.product(HIDDEN_SIZES, (4, 128, 1024)):
+            with self.subTest(hidden_size=hidden_size, num_tokens=num_tokens):
+                torch.manual_seed(num_tokens)
+                hidden_states = torch.randn(
+                    num_tokens, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+                )
+                router_logits = torch.randn(
+                    num_tokens, NUM_EXPERTS, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+                )
+                ref_weights = torch.empty(
+                    num_tokens, TOPK, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32
+                )
+                ref_ids = torch.empty(
+                    num_tokens, TOPK, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+                )
+                ref_weights, ref_ids = aiter_fused_topk(
+                    hidden_states,
+                    router_logits,
+                    TOPK,
+                    True,
+                    topk_ids=ref_ids,
+                    topk_weights=ref_weights,
+                )
+
+                with (
+                    patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter", True),
+                    patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter_topk_gating", True),
+                    patch.object(topk_module, "_is_gfx95", True),
+                    patch.object(
+                        topk_module,
+                        "aiter_fused_topk",
+                        side_effect=AssertionError(
+                            "the legacy launcher should be bypassed"
+                        ),
+                        create=True,
+                    ),
+                ):
+                    weights, ids = topk_module.fused_topk(
+                        hidden_states,
+                        router_logits,
+                        topk=TOPK,
+                        renormalize=True,
+                    )
+
+                # BF16 ties can swap or reorder equal-logit experts.
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    router_logits.gather(1, ids.long()).sort(dim=-1).values,
+                    router_logits.gather(1, ref_ids.long()).sort(dim=-1).values,
+                    rtol=0,
+                    atol=0,
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    weights.sort(dim=-1).values,
+                    ref_weights.sort(dim=-1).values,
+                    rtol=1e-5,
+                    atol=1e-6,
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    weights.sum(dim=-1),
+                    torch.ones(num_tokens, device="cuda"),
+                    rtol=1e-5,
+                    atol=1e-6,
+                )
+
+    def test_dispatch_envelope_is_narrow(self):
+        logits = torch.empty(4, NUM_EXPERTS, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        packed = torch.empty(1, device="cuda")
+        with (
+            patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter", True),
+            patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter_topk_gating", True),
+            patch.object(topk_module, "_is_gfx95", True),
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(_envelope(logits, 4096))
+            for hidden_size in HIDDEN_SIZES:
+                with self.subTest(hidden_size=hidden_size):
+                    self.assertTrue(_envelope(logits, hidden_size))
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(
+                            torch.empty(
+                                topk_module._AITER_TOPK_GATING_MAX_ROWS + 1,
+                                NUM_EXPERTS,
+                                device="cuda",
+                                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                            ),
+                            hidden_size,
+                        )
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(logits, hidden_size, hidden_dtype=torch.float16)
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(
+                            torch.empty(4, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+                            hidden_size,
+                        )
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(_envelope(logits.float(), hidden_size))
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(
+                            torch.empty(
+                                NUM_EXPERTS, 8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+                            ).t(),
+                            hidden_size,
+                        )
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(
+                            logits,
+                            hidden_size,
+                            correction_bias=torch.empty(NUM_EXPERTS, device="cuda"),
+                        )
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        _envelope(logits, hidden_size, num_fused_shared_experts=1)
+                    )
+                    self.assertFalse(_envelope(logits, hidden_size, packed_out=packed))
+        with patch.object(topk_module, "_use_aiter_topk_gating", False):
+            for hidden_size in HIDDEN_SIZES:
+                self.assertFalse(_envelope(logits, hidden_size))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
## v0.5.20 at the default page size

This PR rerun on SGLang v0.5.20 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x`) at the default page size (1), with `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` and `--disable-radix-cache`. 8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4. Same 12 cells as the description: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16.

- **baseline**: stock v0.5.20.[Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), on the same node as the baseline. Server arguments are identical apart from `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING=1`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: stock v0.5.20 plus #39986's router, with its gate widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows. It ran on a second MI355X node against a stock v0.5.20 rerun on that node, so its row is the ratio to that rerun. Stock differs by 0.26% without MTP and 0.01% with MTP between the two nodes.

MTP arms also carry #39064 and #39069 so NEXTN loads this checkpoint. Ratios are candidate / baseline geomeans over the 12 cells. TTFT is median TTFT, so below 1.0 is faster.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| **this PR** | **1.0103** | 1.0000 |
| #39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0129 | 0.9990 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~3.99 | 1.0000 |
| **this PR** | **1.0040** | ~3.99 | 0.9912 |
| #39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0051 | ~3.99 | 1.0039 |

Accept length is 3.979-3.997 per cell for this PR's pair (mean 3.987 baseline, 3.985 this PR) and 3.976-3.998 for the Triton pair (mean 3.984 stock, 3.986 Triton).

What differs from the v0.5.19 numbers in the description (page size 64, +1.48% / +2.22%):

- The gain is smaller, and MTP now gains less than non-MTP (+0.40% against +1.03%). A likely reason is that the MTP step is longer at page size 1, so the same per-step router saving is a smaller share of it. This has not been profiled.
- The Triton arm is 0.26% above this PR without MTP and 0.11% above with MTP. That is the same size as the stock difference between the two nodes, so the two routers still tie end to end.
- The no-ceiling arm and the kernel-count table were not rerun. They are v0.5.19 only.

Microbenchmark on v0.5.20, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.00 | **11.77** | 20.73 | 9.36 | 4.76 | **4.08** |
| 1024 | 15.48 | **12.07** | 20.64 | 9.40 | 5.48 | **4.76** |
| 2048 | 15.18 | **12.28** | 20.86 | 9.46 | 9.67 | **6.54** |
| 4096 | 15.09 | **12.25** | 20.73 | 11.43 | 11.55 | **10.63** |
| 5120 | 15.20 | **12.49** | 20.76 | **11.46** | 12.86 | 12.58 |
| 6144 | 15.20 | **13.78** | 20.83 | **11.62** | 14.14 | 14.74 |
| 7168 | 15.25 | 15.18 | 20.64 | **11.60** | 15.41 | 16.64 |
| 8192 | **15.15** | 16.42 | 20.65 | **11.83** | 16.96 | 18.52 |
| 16384 | **19.11** | 28.64 | 32.37 | **18.67** | 28.85 | 32.81 |

The v0.5.19 conclusions hold:

- On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.86 vs 11.46 us, 28.85 vs 18.67 at 16384).
- Eager, it stays ahead through 6144 and ties legacy at 7168 (15.18 vs 15.25 us, within run-to-run spread).
- Under graphs, Triton leads `topk_gating` by about 0.7 us per call up to 1024 rows.

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) (the stock v0.5.20 image), graph `topk_gating` is 8.04 / 9.23 / 9.66 / 11.65 us at 1 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 rows, so the generic-kernel fallback is unchanged. Legacy and Triton in that image match the table above within 0.6 us.

## v0.5.21 with aiter main and fused shared experts

On v0.5.21 with aiter main and #41899's fused shared expert, this PR gives +1.50% output throughput without MTP and +0.71% with MTP. On v0.5.20 it was +1.03% / +0.40%. 

Setup: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x`, aiter main `a786bda2` (it has [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334) and [Rocm/aiter5835](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5835), so no aiter patch), #41899 with `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`, and #39069 for NEXTN. 8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, page size 1, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`, `--disable-radix-cache`, same 12 cells as the description. Both arms ran on one node. The only difference is this PR plus `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING=1`. MTP arms use `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` with `SGLANG_AITER_HONOR_EXPLICIT_MEM_FRACTION=1`, non-MTP uses 0.9. The baseline router is `topkGatingSoftmax`. #39986's Triton router is in v0.5.21 but fires only at hidden size 4096 and at most 128 rows, so not for this model.

Ratios are this PR / baseline, geomean over the 12 cells:

| Mode | out tok/s | median TTFT | median ITL | accept length (baseline / this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| non-MTP | **1.0150** | 0.9953 | 0.9766 | - |
| NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens | **1.0071** | 0.9800 | 0.9903 | 3.988 / 3.985 |

- Without MTP, this PR is ahead in all 12 cells, from +4.6% at 8k/1k concurrency 4 to +0.3% at 60k/600 concurrency 64.
- With MTP, it is ahead in 10 of 12 cells, up to +3.8% at 8k/1k concurrency 4. The other two (8k/1k concurrency 256, 60k/600 concurrency 64) are -0.1%, within run-to-run spread.
- The gain is larger than on v0.5.20, but the kernel did not get faster: graph legacy and graph `topk_gating` match the v0.5.20 times within 0.15 us. 
- Fusion: on ROCm, Qwen appends the shared slot after top-k (`fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights`, which also computes the shared gate). The router logits stay 512 wide, `TopK` has no fused shared experts, and `topk_gating` runs.

Microbenchmark on v0.5.21 with aiter main, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router as it ships in v0.5.21. 5120 to 7168 rows were not rerun.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.57 | **12.70** | 24.41 | 9.22 | **4.75** | 4.99 |
| 1024 | 16.12 | **13.13** | 24.94 | 9.36 | **5.46** | 5.53 |
| 2048 | 16.07 | **12.97** | 24.87 | 9.47 | 9.66 | **7.25** |
| 4096 | 16.04 | **13.08** | 24.83 | 11.57 | 11.60 | **11.41** |
| 8192 | **15.97** | 16.62 | 24.94 | **11.72** | 16.81 | 19.56 |
| 16384 | **19.00** | 28.48 | 34.16 | **18.72** | 29.49 | 35.16 |

- Under graphs, `topk_gating` beats legacy through 1024 rows, is within 0.2 us at 2048 and 4096, and loses from 8192. The 4096-row ceiling stays.
- Eager, it beats legacy through 4096 rows and loses at 8192.
- Triton is 0.7 to 0.9 us slower under graphs than on v0.5.20, so `topk_gating` now leads it through 1024 rows. Triton still leads at 2048 and 4096.
- Routed weights match legacy within 1.2e-7. Above 1024 rows a few ids differ, only where two experts tie on the same bf16 score at the top-10 edge.
